anti_overlap: Owns the phase-ORDER/assembly-sequence correctness of step_cycle and the two-engine COMPOSITION/interface-fit question; the metrology lens owns the NUMERIC fidelity of the port and the standard-DRIFT of the duplicated Bp, not the joint order.

Owns the CUJ-completeness audit (missing recruitment, roost, interrupt, roster gate; WI-4 over-building v2 spatial into v1) as MISSING/MISPLACED MEMBERS; the metrology lens owns unit-reconciliation and quantization error, not which CUJ members are absent.

Frames the INDIRECT-vs-DIRECT control contradiction and the dropped 'vise' as reproducing-from-an-offcut (structural joint identity); the metrology lens touches the vise only insofar as its float arithmetic quantizes badly, not whether the control MODEL is faithful.
Reasons in members, joints, datums, assembly sequence, and raising; the metrology lens reasons in standards, calibration chains, rounding rules, and unit systems — no shared primitive vocabulary.
decision_lens: Would a master joiner sign off that these separately-cut members will raise into one frame — or flag a joint order that cannot close, a shared datum that was never agreed, a 'test joint' that proves fit against a member from the same bench (proving nothing), a reference member that is actually a retired offcut, or a frame with no member-replacement joint for the piece the CUJ says WILL be replaced? Rank by whether the flaw prevents the frame from raising at all (P0), guarantees a bad seat at composition (P1), degrades the joint (P2), or is finish-planing (P3).
distance_rationale: A centuries-refined manual craft of cutting wooden members on independent benches so they compose into one nail-less frame is causally unrelated to Rust engine architecture, yet it is precisely the discipline of independent-fabrication-that-must-later-compose: assembly sequence that only fails at raising (the phase-order bug), a shared reference datum without which two benches' members never seat (the two-engine composition and cycle/week datum), joints that look structural but bear no load (the WI-8 agnosticism fig leaf), reproducing a member from the true master versus a warped offcut (the port fidelity of the TS 'vise'), and designing a member-replacement joint (recruitment-after-death). It is not on the banned list and shares no parent discipline with historical metrology.
expected_isomorphisms: step_cycle five-phase order <-> timber-raising assembly sequence that only reveals an impossible joint-order at the raising
two engines composed later + cycle/week mismatch <-> two members cut on separate benches with no agreed shared datum, guaranteeing they don't seat
WI-8 second-vocabulary test on the same bench <-> a decorative test joint fitted to a mortise the same hand cut — proves self-consistency, not that an independent member seats
port dropping riskAppetite/vise + DIRECT dispatch replacing INDIRECT disposition <-> reproducing a member from a warped offcut and calling it the master joint
no recruitment work item vs ratified 'a dead bird needs replacement' <-> a frame with no member-replacement joint for the very member the design says will fail and be replaced
focus: Whether two engines cut on independent benches (animal-sim, city-sim) and the agnostic-substrate/vocabulary joint will actually seat into one frame later — assembly-sequence (phase-order) correctness, interface tolerances, and whether the reference member being reproduced is the true master or a discarded offcut.
name: fd-joinery-composition-fit
persona: Apply the perspective of a traditional timber-frame joiner working in the scribe-rule and square-rule traditions — the pre-modern craft (Japanese kigumi, European scribe carpentry) of cutting mortise-and-tenon members on separate benches so that when raised they lock into one rigid frame with no glue, no nails, and no master jig holding it. This craft reasons about: the assembly SEQUENCE (which member must be inserted before which, or the frame cannot close — a joint order that only reveals its impossibility at raising), interface tolerance and reference faces (every member is cut relative to a datum; two benches must share the datum or nothing seats), the difference between a joint that carries load and a decorative joint that only looks structural, reproducing a member faithfully from a story-pole reference versus from a warped offcut, and designing a joint so a single member can be replaced without dismantling the whole frame. It is the discipline of independent-fabrication-that-must-compose, judged only at raising.
review_areas: Assembly-sequence correctness of step_cycle's phase order (WI-7: dispatch -> return -> drain -> breakdown -> death): a joiner checks whether inserting members in this order can close the frame — does draining AFTER resolving returns but the breakdown check reading post-drain state, then a death check with a multi-cycle grace, compose without a member trapped or double-counted (e.g. a bird that both foraged-to-restore this cycle AND is checked for starvation-death on the same cycle's drained value; a refusal that mutates state the death check then re-reads)?

The shared-datum problem for the two engines (R1 save=replay across future composition): scribe-rule members from two benches only seat if they share a reference datum — animal-sim keys its own RNG domain (domain 1) independent of city-sim's domain 6 and steps in 'cycles' while city-sim steps in 'weeks'; when the composition engine steps BOTH, what is the shared datum (the seed derivation, the tick boundary, the order of the two sub-steps) and does building animal-sim's step_cycle signature (seed, state, dispatches) WITHOUT a run-identity/config wrapper foreclose seating it into city-sim's step_week_run(config, commands) -> CityRun shape?

The WI-8 agnosticism joint — load-bearing or decorative: the test cuts a SECOND 'rat' vocabulary on the SAME bench (same author, same session, from the same public API the raven vocab used) and raises it through the same engine — a joiner notes that fitting two tenons YOU cut to a mortise YOU cut proves your own consistency, not that an independent member will seat; what raven-shaped assumption is silently the datum (fixed Needs = food/water/health/interest struct, Atmosphere enum's Cold/Neutral/Hot, the Need { Food, Water } binary, the single 'forage' verb) that a genuinely foreign vocabulary (octopus: no 'cold', 8 limbs, ink, dens) would split against?

Reproducing from the master vs an offcut (the port premise): the plan reproduces lib/cycle.ts as 'proven-but-authoritative' — but a joiner insists on cutting to the STORY POLE, not a warped scrap; the plan's WI-3 reproduces a strictly SIMPLER member than the TS master (it drops riskAppetite, chosenSource, the dodge roll, FORAGE_RELIEF_SCALE, REST_RELIEF, the disposition-bends-behavior 'vise' that IS the design's soul per cycle.ts decisions 1/3/4) and REPLACES the player's INDIRECT disposition-verb with a DIRECT 'send bird to this specific ground' Dispatch — is the plan reproducing the proven joint or a different, cruder joint labeled with the same name?

The member-replacement joint that the frame requires but the plan omits: ravenous-00b's ratified closed decision states 'a dead bird needs replacement/recruitment' and grief scars on survivors — a joiner designs the frame so a failed member can be knocked out and a new one driven in; the plan's WI-7 kills birds (Dead state) but has NO work item for recruitment/replacement, so the frame permanently loses members with no joint to add one — does the plan raise a frame that can only shrink?

Interface tolerance at the vocabulary/engine seam and the CUJ under-cut: ravenous-04's R5 closed decision defers SPATIAL forage fields to v2 ('v1 = scalar drains + one forage verb; spatial forage/thermal/roost-siting fields deferred to v2'), yet WI-4 builds the full spatial bloom/decay/position field into v1 — a joiner flags a member cut to the wrong dimension for its slot; is the plan cutting a v2 member into the v1 mortise (over-building), while simultaneously OMITTING v1 members the CUJ demands (roost, night-exposure threat, curated pause-and-zoom interrupt, the roster/availability gate that is ravenous-04's spine)?
severity_examples: P0: WI-7 phase order resolves a returning forager's restore in step 2 and drains needs in step 3, but the death check in step 5 reads food AFTER the drain — a bird that foraged this cycle and a bird that never left can hit the same drained value, and because the plan never specifies whether a foraging bird ALSO drains while away (does the away-bird pay livingCost each of its N cycles out?), the frame's central load path (survive-by-foraging) is under-specified and a coding agent will guess, corrupting the whole survival trajectory the design is about.

P1: the ratified ravenous-00b decision 'a dead bird needs replacement/recruitment' has no work item, so the built frame can only lose members — a session where the flock dwindles to zero has no recovery joint, contradicting a closed CUJ decision the plan claims to serve; this must be a work item (even a stub) before execution, not a follow-up.

P1: step_cycle's signature (seed, state, dispatches) omits the run-identity/config wrapper city-sim's step_week_run(config, commands) -> CityRun carries, so the composition plan will have to re-cut animal-sim's boundary member to seat it — the datum was never shared, guaranteeing rework at raising; either share the datum now or the 'no dependency between engines' stance is a deferred integration debt, not a clean separation.
source_domain: Traditional timber-frame joinery (scribe-rule and square-rule carpentry; Japanese kigumi mortise-and-tenon framing raised without glue, nails, or a master jig)
success_hints: Read lib/cycle.ts in full and list what WI-3 DROPS versus the TS master: riskAppetite, chosenSource, the boldness-scaled dodge roll, FORAGE_RELIEF_SCALE, REST_RELIEF, and the three Dispositions (forage-bold/forage-cautious/rest) — then judge whether the plan's Dispatch{animal, ground} (player picks the exact ground) reproduces or CONTRADICTS the TS's decision 1 (INDIRECT: player sets a disposition, the BIRD self-selects the source), which the plan's own 'Mental models' section quotes as decision 7 'you never puppet it.'

Read ../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim/src/sim.rs around step_week_run (line ~2883) and its RunConfig/RunIdentity/CityRun types to see the boundary shape animal-sim must eventually seat against — then judge whether step_cycle's leaner signature is a clean sibling or a member cut to a different datum.

Walk the WI-7 five-phase order as an assembly sequence with a concrete two-bird trace (one foraging-and-returning, one idle-and-starving) and look for a member that is trapped, double-restored, or death-checked on a value the previous phase already mutated; the ordering bug, if any, only shows at the raising.

For WI-8, enumerate the raven-shaped datums baked into the 'agnostic' cast.rs/needs.rs (the fixed four-field Needs struct, Atmosphere's Cold/Neutral/Hot, Need{Food,Water}, single forage verb, effective_boldness reading traits+scars) and test each against the named future vocabularies (octopus, rats) the plan says must reuse it — a datum that only fits mammalian-flock animals makes WI-8 a decorative joint.

Cross-check EVERY ratified closed_decision in ravenous-00b and ravenous-04 against the work items: flag each closed decision with no corresponding WI (recruitment/replacement, roost, night-exposure, curated interrupt, roster/availability gate, the R5 'spatial deferred to v2' that WI-4 violates) — these are missing or misplaced members the frame is specified to have.

Separate raising-blockers (frame cannot close: phase-order under-spec, missing recruitment joint, INDIRECT-vs-DIRECT control contradiction) from finish work (naming, doc notes); the joiner only escalates what stops the raise.
task_context: Adversarially review this execution-grade build plan for RaveNous's survival floor BEFORE a coding agent executes it. The plan creates a new deterministic Rust crate 'animal-sim' as a vocabulary-agnostic substrate (needs/foraging/scars/permadeath; raven is the first vocabulary, octopus/rats are future vocabularies). It ports a proven-but-retired TypeScript survival loop (lib/cycle.ts, lib/flock.ts, lib/fields/food.ts) into fixed-point Rust. Focus the lenses on: (1) is the animal-sim/city-sim separation correct — no dependency + duplicated Bp fixed-point, or a drift trap? (2) is determinism airtight given the ruling that a save = deterministic replay, when two engines with independent seed streams must later be composed? (3) is porting truncating-integer basis points (float 0.28 -> Bp 2800) behavior-preserving vs the TS floats? (4) is the WI-8 vocabulary-agnosticism test a real proof or a fig leaf — what raven assumption leaks into the 'agnostic' engine? (5) is step_cycle's phase order (dispatch->return->drain->breakdown->death) free of ordering bugs? (6) is the 'cycle' vs city-sim 'week' time-unit mismatch a landmine deferred too casually? (7) what do the ratified CUJs (docs/cujs/ravenous-00*, ravenous-04) demand that the plan is missing — recruitment-after-death has no work item, the interest mechanic is a formula-less provisional. Rank findings by severity and flag block-execution vs follow-up. The ratified CUJs and the city-sim engine (../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim/src/) are the ground truth.
